scope: Real photographs of exactly the named mission hardware for an educational web simulation. IDs are NORAD catalog numbers supplied by the site. Cropped and downsampled in WebP.
reuse: NASA media guidelines specifically allow educational/informational uses and attribution; LROC permits educational use with credit NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University. All website and title credits are kept in index.json.

22077.name: KITSAT-1 / 우리별 1호
22077.reason: Checked original KAIST/SaTReC program page, which states all rights reserved. Korean government anniversary press material specifies text-only free-use terms and warns its photos are separately licensed. No explicitly reusable photograph of the actual flight spacecraft located in this search.

notes.50463: In-flight engineering pupil image made by NIRCam of its own real primary mirror segments, not an exterior artist rendering. Credit NASA/STScI. Original page credit text is in the linked caption.
notes.53365: Northbound/southbound lunar orbital flyby. The dim elongated spacecraft is the observed feature, as explained in the NASA release. Its physical outline is not resolved. The 16-bit source was scaled linearly to 8-bit gray, cropped around the feature, and reduced for display.
notes.10321: NASA Kennedy catalog description names Voyager-1 specifically; the photo predates its September 5 launch. Do not label as photographed in flight.
